meta.title: Daly 1864 reconciled calibration set
meta.source: Cesar Daly, L'Architecture privee au XIXme siecle sous Napoleon III, Serie 1, Vol. 1 t.2 (1864); Polona scans, 1920 px wide
meta.unit_of_observation: BUILDING, not plate. Plate counts overstate the sample: 6 Premiere plates cover 4 buildings (two elevation/section pairs), 11 Deuxieme elevation plates cover 10 buildings (26 rue Bergere was measured twice).
meta.method: Per-plate scale from the graduated metre bar (1:100 elevations, larger for details); printed dimension callouts preferred over pixel measurement wherever they exist.

printed_callout_coverage.Premiere Classe: 125 Champs-Elysees full storey ladder (section); 119 Champs-Elysees porte cochere plan width 2.600
printed_callout_coverage.Deuxieme Classe: 2-4 Sebastopol door chain 2.950/0.700/1.360; 87 Sebastopol door width 1.760; 9 Conservatoire door width 1.630 and window chain 2.100/1.800/0.800/0.300; 88 Rivoli balcony projection 0.600; 120 Sebastopol console 0.590; 2-4 Sebastopol croisee width 1.300
printed_callout_coverage.Troisieme Classe: NONE - both plates are scale-bar only

duplicate_reading_error.subject: 26 rue Bergere, plate daly_elevation_34, measured independently in two work packages

disagreement.storey_labelling: reading A calls the 3.09 m level a low 1er etage, reading B calls it an entresol - same physical band, opposite role
disagreement.storey_heights: up to 0.36 m (9%) on individual storeys

duplicate_reading_error.conclusion: Horizontal extents and total heights reproduce to under 1%. The DATUM decisions - where the floor line is, where the cornice ends and the comble begins, what role a storey plays - carry 5-20% error. Every derived proportion inherits that.

other_internal_conflicts: 120 Sebastopol door: 1.80 x 3.40 m from the elevation, 1.61 x 3.35 m from its own detail plate 57 (11% on width).
119 Champs-Elysees porte cochere: 2.99 m measured off the elevation against a PRINTED 2.600 m on the plan - a 15% error in a scale-bar width reading, and the best available bound on that error.
119 Champs-Elysees storeys: elevation 1er 3.35 / 2e 4.30 versus detail plate 78 sill-to-sill 1er 3.99 / 2e 3.80, which reverses which storey is taller.
Avenue de l'Imperatrice: elevation and section (plate 61) give irreconcilable floor levels; the source declined to publish street-elevation storey heights.

Premiere Classe.caveat: Source flags every floor level UNCERTAIN: floor lines are not drawn, datum inferred from balcony rails and entablature bands.

INTERNAL CONFLICT: elevation gives 1er 3.35 / 2e 4.30 f-f; detail plate 78 gives sill-to-sill 1er 3.99 / 2e 3.80, which reverses which storey is taller. Bay pitch also disagrees (3.49 elevation vs 3.79 detail).

Premiere Classe.door_height_note: two-storey arched carriage arch; OUTLIER, not a door height in the ordinary sense
Premiere Classe.caveat: Source declined to publish street-elevation storey heights: elevation and companion section (plate 61) cannot be reconciled. Only 2 etage heights, both from the section.

Deuxieme Classe.caveat: rez and entresol split is UNCERTAIN (one shopfront frame); their sum, 6.074 m, is MEASURED.

Deuxieme Classe.door_width_alt_source: detail plate 06, same door, independent reading
Deuxieme Classe.caveat: No mansard and no entresol: masonry attic behind a balustrade. Facade width UNCERTAIN. Lowest cornice in the corpus (14.78 m).

MEASURED TWICE, independently, in two different work packages. Values above are the mean of the two readings. See meta.duplicate_reading_error for the disagreement, which is the corpus's own error bar.

2e etage is a colossal order embracing the etage plus a low mezzanine (5.48 m composite); its split into 2.88 + 2.60 is UNCERTAIN. Bay pitch 2.09 m reflects unusually narrow trumeaux and should not drive bay-pitch calibration.
ZERO STOREY TAPER: 1er, 2e and 3e are exactly 3.20 m, verified three ways. Facade width UNCERTAIN (corner building). Door width disagrees 11% between the elevation and its own detail plate.
Cleanest monotonic taper in the corpus (0.89, 0.85, 0.74). Carriage arch swallows rez AND entresol, hence the 5.00 m height.
Bell-profile mansard holding two levels of accommodation: comble is 28% of total height.
Detail plates only; no elevation measured. Contributes a door, nothing else.

Troisieme Classe.facade_width_note: per house; three adjoining houses 8.63/8.54/8.53, total composition 25.70 m
Troisieme Classe.note: Neighbour alignment: floor lines, string courses, cornice, both balcons filants and the roof match across all three houses to within 0.05-0.12 m. Bay COUNT differs (3/4/3), levels do not.
No entresol, no dormers, no habitable comble, NO projecting balcony anywhere - flush garde-corps only. Top etage wall height drops to 2.20 m.

ladder.verdict: Falls only 9% across the whole ladder while the ranges overlap almost completely (Deuxieme 3.42-4.85 spans every other class entirely). Treat as class-independent.

storey_height_ground.notes: The single most stable absolute in the corpus after the door. 16 buildings, 3.42-4.85 m, median 3.95 m. The one extreme (4.85 m, Rivoli 88) is a deliberate tall-boutique type, not measurement error.

storey_height_entresol.definition: Entresol floor-to-floor where an entresol exists.

ladder.verdict: Not a ladder quantity: no Premiere or Troisieme building in this corpus has an entresol at all. The PRESENCE of the entresol is the class signal, not its height.

storey_height_entresol.notes: 9 of 10 Deuxieme buildings have one; 0 of 4 Premiere and 0 of 2 Troisieme do. Median 2.98 m, range 2.40-3.12 m. Entresol/ground ratio median 0.775 (range 0.585-0.871, n=9).

storey_height_compressed_level.definition: Height of the squeezed level between the ground storey and the tallest etage (entresol where one exists, otherwise a low 1er etage).

ladder.verdict: Present in 14 of the 16 buildings with measured storeys; absent in BOTH Troisieme buildings. Premiere median 3.40 m (n=4), Deuxieme 2.975 m (n=10), Troisieme none (n=0).

storey_height_compressed_level.recommendation: SOURCED as a PATTERN, WEAK as a number
storey_height_compressed_level.notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: a compressed level sits between the commercial ground storey and the noble floor in every Premiere and Deuxieme building measured. In Premiere it is dressed as a full 1er etage (3.20-3.60 m); in Deuxieme it is an entresol (2.40-3.12 m). Troisieme has no such level and no noble floor. Ratio of noble floor to compressed level: Premiere median 1.25, Deuxieme median 1.30.

storey_height_principal.definition: Floor-to-floor of the tallest etage (piano nobile).

ladder.verdict: THE CLEAREST LADDER IN THE CORPUS. 4.23 / 3.83 / 3.04 m. The Premiere-Troisieme gap (1.2 m) is far larger than the duplicate-reading error (0.2 m).

storey_height_principal.recommendation: SOURCED for the ORDERING; SOURCED for the Deuxieme distribution; WEAK for Premiere and Troisieme values
storey_height_principal.notes: Premiere n=4 but three of those four have source-flagged uncertain floor lines, so the Premiere median rests effectively on one printed plate. Deuxieme n=10 is solid. Troisieme n=2 but its two values are 3.00 and 3.07 - remarkably tight.

storey_height_uppers.definition: Floor-to-floor of every etage above the piano nobile (one observation per storey, not per building).

ladder.verdict: 3.48 / 3.07 / 2.92 m. Monotonic, but Troisieme rests on n=2 storeys from one building and the Deuxieme-Troisieme step (0.15 m) is inside the duplicate-reading error bar.

storey_height_uppers.notes: Observation counts are storeys, not buildings: 6 / 25 / 2, and the Troisieme count of 2 comes from a single building (rue de Longchamps has no etage above its tallest, so it contributes none). Treat the Troisieme figure as anecdote. Deuxieme spread is wide (2.32-3.83 m) because the corpus contains both zero-taper facades (120 Sebastopol, three storeys at exactly 3.20 m) and hard-tapering ones (39 Mathurins, 4.15 -> 2.32 m).

storey_taper_ratio.definition: Geometric-mean storey-to-storey ratio counted UPWARD FROM the piano nobile (not from the 1er, which is often the compressed level).

ladder.direction: weakens down the class ladder (Premiere tapers hardest)
ladder.verdict: 0.861 / 0.906 / 0.962 - but Premiere n=3 and Troisieme n=1. NOT SAFE to calibrate the class dependence.

storey_taper_ratio.notes: The Deuxieme distribution (n=10, 0.795-0.993, median 0.906) is usable on its own. Two Deuxieme buildings taper essentially not at all (0.993, 0.992) and one tapers hard (0.795): the generator should sample a distribution, not apply a constant. Measured naively from the 1er upward the ratio is meaningless because the 1er is often the shortest storey.

taper_first_etage_over_ground.definition: Ratio of the first etage above the ground storey to the ground storey.

ladder.verdict: Premiere 0.834, Deuxieme 0.993, Troisieme 0.789. NOT a ladder - the Deuxieme value is high only because the compressed level has been split off as an entresol.

taper_first_etage_over_ground.notes: Included as an explicit warning: this is the ratio a naive generator would use, and it inverts.

ladder.verdict: 2.81 / 2.85 / 2.54 m. Deuxieme sits ABOVE Premiere. The class ladder does not exist in this quantity.

bay_pitch.recommendation: SOURCED as a CORPUS-WIDE RANGE; INSUFFICIENT as a class discriminator
bay_pitch.notes: Corpus range 2.09-3.49 m over 16 buildings; within-class spread (1.5x in both Premiere and Deuxieme) is larger than any between-class difference. Premiere itself runs 2.32 to 3.49 m - 'Premiere Classe' does not mean one bay rhythm. 9 rue du Conservatoire (2.09 m) is flagged by its own source as unrepresentative.

ladder.verdict: 17.05 / 15.61 / 10.42 m. Monotonic, but Premiere and Deuxieme overlap heavily (Deuxieme spans 11.86-19.98 m, containing the whole Premiere range) and Troisieme n=2.

facade_width.notes: The Troisieme drop is real but is partly a plot-width fact rather than a class fact: the Beaumarchais plate is three 8.6 m houses built as one composition.

opening_width_typical.definition: Typical upper-storey croisee masonry opening width, one representative value per building.

ladder.verdict: 1.14 / 1.24 / 1.07 m. Deuxieme is the WIDEST. Corpus-wide 1.04-1.30 m, a 1.25x span across buildings whose facades vary 2.4x in width and whose class rank spans the whole social range.

opening_width_typical.notes: THE STRONGEST ABSOLUTE AFTER THE DOOR. Window width is set by the croisee (the two-leaf French casement), not by the building's grandeur. One value is a printed callout (1.300 m at 2-4 Sebastopol); a second (1.25 m at 9 rue du Conservatoire) is pixel-read on a plate whose scale is fixed by printed callouts. Both agree with the ordinary scale-bar readings.

opening_height_principal.definition: Window opening height at the piano nobile.

ladder.verdict: 2.92 / 2.24 / 2.09 m. Monotonic and the Premiere-Deuxieme step (0.68 m) is large.

opening_height_principal.recommendation: SOURCED for ordering; WEAK for Troisieme values
opening_height_principal.notes: Because width is near-constant, ALL of the class signal in the window is in its height. This is the cleanest statement of the ABSOLUTE/PROPORTIONAL split in the whole dataset.

opening_aspect_principal.definition: Opening height/width at the piano nobile.

ladder.verdict: 2.49 / 2.04 / 1.95. Monotonic; the Deuxieme-Troisieme step (0.09) is inside the noise, the Premiere-Deuxieme step (0.45) is not.

opening_aspect_principal.recommendation: SOURCED for ordering; WEAK for Troisieme
opening_aspect_principal.notes: Premiere spread 2.35-2.83, Deuxieme 1.56-2.45 (overlapping the Premiere floor), Troisieme 1.93-1.96.

opening_aspect_uppers.definition: Opening height/width above the piano nobile (one observation per storey).

ladder.verdict: 1.99 / 1.80 / 1.91. Troisieme sits ABOVE Deuxieme. NOT a usable ladder.

opening_aspect_uppers.notes: Flagged explicitly per the brief. Within-building variation is larger than between-class variation: 9 Conservatoire runs 1.74 down to 1.14 while 63 Sebastopol runs 1.98 / 1.66 / 2.08 in the wrong order.

ladder.verdict: Deuxieme only (n=6, 1.28-1.83). No comparison possible.

opening_aspect_entresol.notes: Detail plates show the entresol window is not one shape: 120 Sebastopol h/w 1.23 (single squat opening) vs 9 Conservatoire h/w 2.32 per light (paired lights).

comble_share.definition: Comble (roof) height divided by total pavement-to-roof-crest height.

ladder.verdict: 0.139 / 0.150 / 0.120. Deuxieme is the highest. Ranges are enormous and overlap completely.

comble_share.notes: DO NOT CALIBRATE. Deuxieme runs 0.120 to 0.285 (2.4x) because the corpus mixes plain mansards with combles containing two full storeys (1 Sebastopol 0.279, 2-4 Sebastopol 0.285). Troisieme runs 0.061 to 0.179 on two buildings - one has a habitable mansard, one has a plain low slate roof. The comble is a TYPE choice, not a class-scaled proportion.

cornice_height_above_pavement.definition: Pavement to the top of the main cornice.

ladder.verdict: 19.11 / 18.90 / 15.79 m. The Premiere-Deuxieme step is 0.21 m - nothing. The step down to Troisieme is 3.1 m and is real.

cornice_height_above_pavement.recommendation: SOURCED for the Troisieme step; WEAK for the Premiere/Deuxieme step
cornice_height_above_pavement.notes: Premiere and Deuxieme are BOTH pressed against the 20 m legal facade maximum of the 1859 decree for wide streets: 6 buildings sit between 19.0 and 20.0 m. That ceiling, not class, is what sets the number. The exception is 88 rue de Rivoli at 14.78 m, which spends its allowance on fewer, taller storeys. Height-to-cornice / facade-width rises down the ladder: 1.19 / 1.27 / 1.57 - the Troisieme facade is proportionally the tallest and narrowest.

cornice_band_depth.definition: Depth of the crowning cornice moulding itself.

ladder.verdict: NO PREMIERE DATA AT ALL (n=0). Deuxieme 0.45 (0.33-0.68, n=8), Troisieme 0.685 (0.45-0.92, n=2). No ladder can be stated.

cornice_band_depth.notes: Half the Deuxieme values are source-flagged UNCERTAIN (the cornice underside cannot be separated from the window pediments below). The Troisieme value is higher than the Deuxieme, which if anything inverts the expected ladder. Leave inferred.

ladder.verdict: 22.55 / 22.78 / 18.03 m. Deuxieme median EXCEEDS Premiere because Deuxieme combles are taller.

total_height.notes: Another quantity where the 20 m cornice ceiling flattens the two upper classes and only Troisieme separates.

door_width.definition: Masonry opening width of the principal entrance.

ladder.verdict: 2.57 / 1.78 / 1.36 m across all doors - BUT this ladder is an artefact of door TYPE, see notes.

door_width.notes: See doors_by_type: the ladder is in WHICH DOOR the class gets, not in how big a given door is.

door_height.definition: Threshold to the head or arch crown of the principal entrance opening.

ladder.verdict: 3.53 / 3.38 / 2.90 m. Monotonic but the spread swamps it: Premiere 3.05-7.30, Deuxieme 2.72-5.07.

door_height.notes: Door HEIGHT is not the stable quantity door WIDTH is, because the opening sometimes swallows the entresol (39 Mathurins 5.00 m, 2-4 Sebastopol 5.01 m, 87 Sebastopol 5.07 m) and sometimes stops at a lintel (9 Conservatoire 2.72 m). The height of the LEAVES is far more stable: 2.95 / 3.25 / 3.55 m on the three buildings where it is separately dimensioned, two of them printed.

balcony_height_above_pavement.definition: Height above pavement of the lowest projecting balcony deck (below 9 m).

ladder.verdict: Deuxieme n=8, median 6.95 m, range 6.55-7.93 m - very tight. Premiere n=2 (4.10 and 8.45 m, which are not the same storey). Troisieme n=1 (7.01 m).

balcony_height_above_pavement.notes: The Deuxieme figure is tight because it is structurally determined: it is ground storey + entresol, i.e. the 1er etage floor. Note the class signal here is PRESENCE, not height: 9 of 10 Deuxieme buildings carry a projecting balcony below 9 m; the rue de Longchamps house has no projecting balcony anywhere on the facade, only flush garde-corps.

balcony_railing_height.definition: Garde-corps height above the balcony deck.

ladder.verdict: 0.87 / 0.97 / 1.03 / 1.07 m across four buildings in two classes. Median 1.00 m, total spread 0.20 m.

balcony_railing_height.recommendation: WEAK (n=4) but a clean absolute candidate
balcony_railing_height.notes: Body-scaled like the door. Companion absolute: balcony PROJECTION from the wall face is 0.600 m printed at 88 rue de Rivoli and 0.590 m printed at 120 Sebastopol - two different buildings, two printed callouts, 2% apart.

doors_by_type._finding: Carriage doors are the same size in Premiere and Deuxieme Classe: 2.41-2.62 m (n=4) against 2.57-2.67 m (n=3), medians 2.57 and 2.58 m, a 0.4% difference on a 7-building sample spanning the two top classes. Pedestrian doors are 1.61-1.91 m in Deuxieme (n=8) and 1.36 m in both Troisieme buildings. Troisieme Classe has NO carriage door in this corpus and Premiere has no pedestrian door. The apparent door-width class ladder is therefore entirely a ladder of ENTITLEMENT (does the house get a carriage entrance?) and not of scaling.

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.evidence: spans Premiere and Deuxieme; one value printed

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.caveat: Troisieme pedestrian doors are 1.36 m on both buildings - narrower than any Deuxieme door. n=2, so WEAK, but the gap is 0.25 m and consistent.

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.evidence: all three classes; one printed callout plus one reading on a printed-scale plate

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.recommendation: SOURCED as a value, WEAK as a distribution

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.evidence: printed '30' repeated on the 125 Champs-Elysees ladder; printed '0.300' at 9 Conservatoire
class ladder is only 9% end to end and ranges overlap

ABSOLUTE_calibrate_as_constants.recommendation: SOURCED as a corpus-wide distribution, INSUFFICIENT as a class discriminator

PROPORTIONAL_scale_with_class.recommendation: SOURCED for ordering, WEAK for Premiere and Troisieme values

PROPORTIONAL_scale_with_class.quantity: window opening height at the nobile

PROPORTIONAL_scale_with_class.recommendation: SOURCED for ordering, WEAK for the Deuxieme-Troisieme step
SOURCED only for the drop to Troisieme; the Premiere/Deuxieme pair is flat because both are pinned to the 20 m legal maximum

PROPORTIONAL_scale_with_class.quantity: presence of an entresol / of a compressed level below the nobile
PROPORTIONAL_scale_with_class.recommendation: SOURCED as a categorical class marker
SOURCED as a categorical class marker
WEAK as a categorical class marker

absolute_vs_proportional.headline: Everything a body touches is absolute and everything a body looks at is proportional. Door width, window width, garde-corps height, balcony projection and floor thickness do not move with class. Storey height above the ground floor, window HEIGHT, opening slenderness and overall facade height do. The window is the cleanest single demonstration: its width varies 1.25x across 16 buildings spanning the whole social range, while its height at the noble floor varies 1.40x between Premiere and Troisieme alone.

limits.sample_size: 4 / 10 / 2 buildings. Any Troisieme claim rests on two elevations by two architects; most are marked WEAK for that reason alone.
limits.premiere_is_thinner_than_it_looks: Of the 4 Premiere buildings, only 125 Champs-Elysees has a printed storey ladder. The other three are source-flagged UNCERTAIN (rue de la Paix: no drawn floor lines), internally contradictory (119 Champs-Elysees), or had their storey heights deliberately withheld (Avenue de l'Imperatrice). Premiere storey-height medians therefore rest on effectively one solid building plus three inferences.
limits.publication_bias: These are plates a luxury architectural journal chose to publish as exemplars, with named architects. They are biased toward the grander, more expensively designed and better-built end of each class. Nothing here describes the median Paris building of 1864, and the Troisieme Classe examples in particular are model tenements, not ordinary ones.
limits.single_date: Every plate is 1864. No evidence at all about drift over the 1850-1914 span; the 20 m cornice ceiling that flattens the Premiere/Deuxieme difference is the 1859 decree, and would move under the 1884 and 1902 rules.
limits.geographic_concentration: 7 of the 17 buildings are on the boulevard de Sebastopol or the rue de Rivoli - one Haussmann corridor built to one set of frontage conditions. Treat the Sebastopol group as a cluster, not as 7 independent samples.
limits.measurement_error: Printed callouts are exact. Scale-bar readings carry ~0.3% from the bar itself but 5-20% from datum ambiguity - see meta.duplicate_reading_error. The worst documented case is a 15% width error at 119 Champs-Elysees, caught only because a printed value existed to check it against. Assume any un-printed width in this file could be 10% wrong and any storey height 0.2-0.4 m wrong.
limits.labelling_is_not_stable: The same physical band was called a low 1er etage by one reader and an entresol by another on the same plate. Storey ROLE assignments in this file are interpretations, not measurements.
limits.derived_quantities_are_worse: Comble share, taper ratios and cornice-band depth are all differences of two uncertain datums, so they carry the sum of two errors. That is why they are the quantities marked INSUFFICIENT.

do_not_calibrate_on: comble_share - non-monotonic, 2.4x within-class spread, and the comble is a type choice not a proportion
cornice_band_depth - zero Premiere observations, half the Deuxieme values source-flagged uncertain, and the Troisieme value inverts the expected ladder
opening_aspect_uppers - non-monotonic across the classes and dominated by within-building variation
taper_first_etage_over_ground - inverts; the naive ratio a generator would reach for
balcony_height_above_pavement in Premiere (n=2, different storeys) or Troisieme (n=1)
the 7.30 m porte cochere height at Avenue de l'Imperatrice - a two-storey arch, not a door
any Troisieme Classe absolute value as a distribution - use the two values for ORDERING only
bay pitch as a class discriminator - it is flat, and 9 rue du Conservatoire (2.09 m) is unrepresentative even within its own class
storey heights at 3 rue de la Paix, 119 Champs-Elysees and Avenue de l'Imperatrice as if they were measurements

WEAK: storey taper ratio (use for ordering only)
opening aspect at the nobile, Deuxieme-to-Troisieme step
INSUFFICIENT: balcony height above pavement outside Deuxieme
bay pitch as a function of class
